citation: "The Kinzie House" — wood engraving, in The Chicago Magazine: The West As It Is, vol. 1 no. 1 (Chicago, March 1857); reprinted by A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1884), where it is captioned as the old Kinzie house about 1833.
author: unidentified engraver
describes_date: about 1832-1833, by the caption the Andreas reprint gives it
repository: Wikimedia Commons, File:Kinzie_House.png; the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_kinzie_house_1833.png (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md), and the same artwork at chicago/pre_fire_v1/media/images/buildings/kinzie_house_1857.png
locator: the whole plate, 687 x 436 px in the copy held here
rights_note: Published 1857 in the United States, out of copyright by age; Commons holds it as public domain.
access_notes: Read off the image file itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2497). Neither the 1857 magazine page nor the Andreas page was reached from the run's container, so no page is cited; the caption's date is the catalogue's reading of the Andreas reprint.
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof running along the river, with two stacks through the ridge, about 0.45 and 0.93 of it from the west gable
the piazza across the whole front on slender posts, under its own flatter roof below the main eave, with a railing between the posts
a door at the middle of the front with windows either side
the picket fence enclosing a green before the piazza, toward the water
four columnar Lombardy poplars in a row along the green's river-side fence, from opposite the house's east half to beyond its east end
a big broad-crowned tree behind the house
what_it_does_not_supply: the house in 1812: it shows it about twenty years later
note: The clearest picture of the piazza and the poplar row. It draws the walls sided and light, which may be a later cladding or the engraver's: the 1812 house is built of squared logs from the texts, and the match record says so.
